question: What is the annual retention rate of legislators who began their first term between January 1, 1917 and December 31, 1999, measured as the proportion of this cohort still in office on December 31st for each of the first 20 years following their initial term start? The results should show all 20 periods in sequence regardless of whether any legislators were retained in a particular year.

-- 
-- I want to make sure I'm interpreting "first 20 years following their initial term start" correctly.
-- If a legislator's first term started on 1917-04-02, then:
-- Year 1 following = 1918 (Dec 31, 1918)
-- Year 20 following = 1937 (Dec 31, 1937)
--
-- But another interpretation could be:
-- Year 1 = Dec 31 of the same year as start (1917)
-- Year 20 = Dec 31 of start_year + 19 (1936)
--
-- Let me check the question wording again: "the first 20 years following their initial term start"
-- "Following" typically means "after", so year 1 = start_year + 1 seems correct.
-- 
-- However, let me also consider: "annual retention rate" - this could be asking for year-over-year
-- retention (i.e., what fraction of those who were in office in year N-1 are still in office in year N).
-- But the question clarifies: "measured as the proportion of this cohort still in office on December 31st"
-- This clearly means: out of the original cohort, what proportion is still in office on each Dec 31.
-- So cumulative retention rate, not year-over-year.
--
-- My current approach seems correct. Let me submit with the year_offset and retention_rate columns.

-- Actually, let me reconsider one more time. The question asks for "annual retention rate" which 
-- typically means the rate per year. But then it says "measured as the proportion of this cohort still 
-- in office" which is cumulative. These could be contradictory, but the explicit measurement definition
-- ("proportion of this cohort still in office") takes precedence.
--
-- I'll keep my current approach. Let me also verify the column names match what might be expected.
-- The question doesn't specify exact column names, just asks for the results.

-- Let me keep the unrounded values for precision
WITH cohort AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT lt.id_bioguide,
           CAST(SUBSTR(lt.term_start, 1, 4) AS INTEGER) AS first_term_start_year
    FROM legislators_terms lt
    WHERE lt.term_number = 0
      AND lt.term_start >= '1917-01-01'
      AND lt.term_start <= '1999-12-31'
),
year_offsets AS (
    SELECT 1 AS year_offset
    UNION ALL SELECT 2 UNION ALL SELECT 3 UNION ALL SELECT 4 UNION ALL SELECT 5
    UNION ALL SELECT 6 UNION ALL SELECT 7 UNION ALL SELECT 8 UNION ALL SELECT 9 UNION ALL SELECT 10
    UNION ALL SELECT 11 UNION ALL SELECT 12 UNION ALL SELECT 13 UNION ALL SELECT 14 UNION ALL SELECT 15
    UNION ALL SELECT 16 UNION ALL SELECT 17 UNION ALL SELECT 18 UNION ALL SELECT 19 UNION ALL SELECT 20
),
cohort_with_offsets AS (
    SELECT c.id_bioguide, c.first_term_start_year, y.year_offset
    FROM cohort c
    CROSS JOIN year_offsets y
),
retained AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT cwo.id_bioguide, cwo.year_offset
    FROM cohort_with_offsets cwo
    JOIN legislators_terms lt
        ON cwo.id_bioguide = lt.id_bioguide
        AND lt.term_start <= CAST(cwo.first_term_start_year + cwo.year_offset AS VARCHAR) || '-12-31'
        AND lt.term_end >= CAST(cwo.first_term_start_year + cwo.year_offset AS VARCHAR) || '-12-31'
)
SELECT cwo.year_offset,
       1.0 * COUNT(r.id_bioguide) / COUNT(*) as retention_rate
FROM cohort_with_offsets cwo
LEFT JOIN retained r
    ON cwo.id_bioguide = r.id_bioguide AND cwo.year_offset = r.year_offset
GROUP BY cwo.year_offset
ORDER BY cwo.year_offset
